title: docs(adr): ADR-0111 — record-share management authority and the verb boundary (#3902)
body:
## What this is

The design decision record for **#3902**. Docs-only — this PR adds `docs/adr/0111-record-share-management-authority-and-verb-boundary.md` and nothing else. It is the agreed plan to fix the two defects #3902 reports (plus several more found while writing it down); the P0 and P1 implementation PRs follow separately per the rollout section.

> ADR number: 0110 was taken on `main` (`0110-action-identity-and-declaration-admission`), so this is **0111**.

## The root cause the ADR names

Record sharing shipped as a **data layer with no authorization layer of its own.** Every share-management route (`/data/:object/:id/shares`, `/sharing/rules`) authenticates the caller and then runs the service under a hard-coded `SYSTEM_CTX` — no record-visibility check, no "may this caller manage sharing", no "does this grant enforce anything". Both #3902 defects reduce to one missing model: sharing has no concept of **who may manage a share** or **which verbs a share level grants.**

## Scope found while writing it (beyond the two in #3902)

- `/sharing/rules` (list/create/get/delete/**evaluate**) is the same unauthorized-service pattern and **worse** — a self-authored rule is an object-wide grant generator.
- `recipient_type` accepts four values (`group`/`position`/`unit_and_subordinates`/`guest`) that **no gate enforces** — ADR-0078 inert metadata on the recipient axis; vocabulary also disagrees across three files.
- `grant()` never checks the object's `sharingModel` — a share on a public/bypass/owner-less object is a row no gate reads (the inverse of #3865).
- Manual upsert clobbers rule-materialised rows (ignores `source`).
- Share links: mint-authority = mere visibility, and a record owner can't revoke a link someone else minted on their record.

## The ten rulings

- **D1** `canManageShares` predicate — MVP: owner + `modifyAllRecords`; DEPTH (hierarchy managers) a named future direction; grant may never exceed the granter's own level (Dataverse rule).
- **D2** enforced in the **service**, not just the route; adds a narrow fail-closed `ISecurityService.hasWriteBypass` probe.
- **D3** verb boundary — a share widens *rows*, never *verbs*; `edit` does **not** grant delete; delete = ownership + depth + Modify All. No new delete level.
- **D4** revoke is symmetric with grant + validates the share belongs to the record; refuses non-`manual` rows.
- **D5** listing is management-gated; "shares that concern me" moves to a self-scoped `/data/sys_record_share`.
- **D6** `/sharing/rules` requires `manage_sharing`, enforced in the service (evaluate included).
- **D7** no inert grants — `recipientType` narrowed to `user`, posture-validated (`controlled_by_parent` refused), manual/rule coexist by `source`.
- **D8** share-link re-share semantics made explicit; a record's share-manager may revoke any link on it.
- **D9** a dedicated `manage_sharing` capability (Salesforce "Manage Sharing" parity) instead of borrowing `manage_platform_settings`.
- **D10** migration: tighten directly, fail closed, with deny-log + `explain` + changelog — no warn-only window, no escape valve.

Grounded against Salesforce / Dataverse / Odoo, which converge on both "who may share" (owner + hierarchy + a Share/Manage-Sharing privilege) and "edit ≠ delete".

## Deliberately out of scope (referenced, not re-decided)

Time-boxed shares (ADR-0091), external/guest identity (ADR-0090 D11 + #2776 item 6), scale hardening (#2776 item 3), request-body schema validation (#3877/#3899).

## Rollout

1. This ADR (Proposed → Accepted).
2. **P0 PR** — the authorization face (D1/D2/D4/D5/D6/D7/D9), with the #3902 reproduction (Mallory ①②③) as integration tests.
3. **P1 PR** — the verb boundary (D3); breaking, carries the changelog entry.
4. Follow-ups — share-link rulings (D8), DEPTH management extension.

## Testing

None — documentation only.
